explain.say: Penguins cannot fly in air, but underwater they fly. Their wings have become stiff, flat flippers that they flap to drive themselves through the sea.

explain.say: Unlike a duck paddling with its feet, a penguin beats its flippers, and both the downstroke and the upstroke push it forward, because water is dense enough to push against both ways.

explain.say: A torpedo-shaped body, short tight feathers and tucked-in feet keep drag low. Gentoo penguins, the fastest swimmers, can burst to about 35 kilometres per hour.

explain.say: Penguin bones are solid and heavy instead of hollow, which helps them dive instead of bobbing at the surface. Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 metres and stay under for more than 20 minutes.

faq.q: How do penguins swim so fast?
faq.a: Penguins flap their stiff flippers like wings, getting thrust on both the downstroke and the upstroke. Their smooth, torpedo-shaped bodies slip through the water with little drag.
asks: How fast can a penguin swim?
Do penguins use their feet to swim?

faq.q: Why can't penguins fly in the air?
faq.a: Their wings are too short and stiff, and their bodies too heavy, to make enough lift in thin air. Over millions of years their ancestors traded flying in air for flying in water, which is far denser.

faq.q: Why are penguins shaped like torpedoes?
faq.a: A smooth body that is thick in the middle and tapers at both ends lets water flow around it with little swirling, so there is less drag. Short, overlapping feathers keep the surface smooth.
asks: What shape is best for swimming?

faq.a: Emperor penguins dive deepest, with records of over 500 metres and dives lasting more than 20 minutes. Most of their dives are shallower and shorter.
asks: How long can a penguin hold its breath?

faq.q: Why do penguins leap out of the water?
faq.a: Penguins often porpoise, leaping like dolphins, to breathe without slowing down. Emperor penguins release a cloud of bubbles from their feathers to speed up just before rocketing onto the ice.
asks: How do penguins jump onto ice?

facts: The deepest emperor penguin dive recorded is about 564 metres.
Unlike most flying birds, penguins have solid, dense bones.

quiz.say: Which feature helps penguins dive rather than float at the surface?
quiz.show: Which feature helps penguins dive rather than float at the surface?
quiz.why: Dense bones make penguins heavier for their size, so they dive more easily.

wrong.1: Hollow bones would make them float, which is why flying birds have them.
wrong.2: Penguins have short, stiff flippers, not long wings.

quiz.say: Why can a penguin get thrust on its upstroke too?
quiz.show: Why can a penguin get thrust on its upstroke too?

options.show: Water is dense enough to push against both ways
options.say: Water is dense enough to push against both ways

options.show: Its feet kick at the same time
options.say: Its feet kick at the same time

quiz.why: Dense water resists the flipper in both directions, so both strokes push the penguin forward.

wrong.1: The flippers stay stiff and flat; they do not fold.
wrong.2: Penguin feet mostly steer; the flippers give the thrust.
